Failure to object is evidence only within actual scrutiny, not proof that all objections are exhausted.
The Cartesian-circle reply distinguishes current intuition and later memory; its adequacy is not ruled upon. Everyday scenes belong to these essays, not the historical book.
Latin declinavi and French parer à do not establish a hard opposition between evasion and direct engagement, defeat or translator tampering.
Mind/body roles, genuine respect and reported victory can coexist without diagnosing hypocrisy.
Revius is an opposing intermediary quoted by later editors; lost abstracts and unrecorded intentions remain unknown. The two music examples perform different jobs.
Requesting omission, later permission to print and authorial approval are distinct. The 1647 and 1904 arrangements appeal to different moments without supplying hidden motives.
SAE marginal comparisons remain independently optional and expressly not proofs. Full edition notes and historical source titles/URLs remain separate, not replaced by a common theory-paper citation.
